title: Cartridge manifest (integrity, provenance, updates)
description: Signed, content-addressed record of what a cartridge (or a weight-only update to one) actually contains, per 'Integrity, provenance, and weight-only updates' in index.adoc. The manifest, not the descriptor, is the thing a host verifies before load; the descriptor is what a host routes on. Signatures cover sha256(canonical_json(manifest without 'signatures')). v2: per-artifact license + derived_from (ADR-004), effective_license, provenance.evaluation (the weight-update regression gate).

effective_license.description: The cartridge's effective license (same value as the descriptor's `license`): must be satisfiable given every artifact's `license` below (ADR-004). 'NOASSERTION' = unremediated, fails conformance by design.

kind.description: 'cartridge' = a full, loadable base (runtime + model + descriptor, etc). 'weights-update' = a weight-only delta that MUST carry a 'base' pin.

id.description: Same id as the cartridge this manifest describes or updates (see cartridge-descriptor.schema.json#id).

descriptor_digest.description: Digest of the canonicalized capability descriptor. Required when kind=cartridge; optional on a weights-update (only meaningful if the update also revises measured performance).

base.description: Required when kind=weights-update. Pins the exact base this update applies to, BY DIGEST — never by a mutable version tag — so a host can refuse to apply an update against anything but the artifact it actually installed.

producer.description: What built this, and its version.

inputs.description: Build inputs worth recording for audit (source model digest, calibration set digest, ...).

training.description: Only meaningful when kind=weights-update produced by a training/aggregation round (e.g. federated learning).

dp_epsilon.description: Differential-privacy budget for this round, if applied.

evaluation.description: v2, the weight-update regression gate (index.adoc 'Verification gate'): a weight update is SUPPOSED to change outputs, so parity-vs-previous is vacuous — what must hold is the task metric on a pinned eval set. Required by policy for kind=weights-update; a degradation ships only with an explicit waiver.

baseline.description: Metric with the PREVIOUS weights, same eval set.

waiver.description: Present only when value is worse than baseline: the recorded justification for shipping anyway. Never ship a degradation silently.

blueprint.description: v0.4 (SKEEP-007, ADR-015): set when this cartridge was materialized from a blueprint — which recipe produced these bytes. `digest` is the sha256 of the blueprint file and is what makes `version` mean exactly one recipe.

materialization.description: v0.4: how the blueprint was executed. `profile_digest` pins the materialization profile without publishing it (a private profile stays private; its digest still makes the build auditable to whoever holds it). `toolchain` records the versions ACTUALLY used, which equal the blueprint's pins unless a substitution is being declared.

target.description: Id of the blueprint target that was materialized.

keyid.description: Identifies the public key in the host's trust store. Never resolved from data inside this manifest.

signer.description: Human-readable role/identity, e.g. 'publisher' or 'federated-aggregator'. The trust store, not this field, is authoritative on what the key is authorized to sign (OQ6).

signature.description: Base64-encoded raw signature bytes over sha256(canonical_json(manifest without 'signatures')).

license.description: v2, required (ADR-004): this artifact's license — SPDX where possible, 'proprietary', 'community-restricted', or 'NOASSERTION' (which the license gate fails by design). The cartridge's effective_license must satisfy ALL of these.

derived_from.description: v2 (ADR-004): what upstream this artifact descends from — the compiled NPU blob derives from an upstream checkpoint, a baked-in blob derives from its source model. This is how license obligations trace through builds.

encryption.description: Optional. Confidentiality is independent of the signature above, which covers integrity/authenticity of the (possibly still-encrypted) bytes. See 'Encrypted weights' — modeled on SKaiNET Minerva's device-key pattern: the key itself is never in the manifest, only a reference the host resolves via its own provisioning.

key_ref.description: Opaque key identifier/slot resolved by the host's own key provisioning (secure element, device key store) — not a key or key material.

delivery.description: Optional (ADR-009). Marks this artifact as eligible for platform-native deferred delivery (Google Play Asset Delivery, Apple On-Demand Resources / Background Assets) instead of being bundled into the initial app install — a build-packaging hint, not a change to how the artifact is verified. Absent means 'bundled at install time', the only behavior prior manifests express.

timing.description: Play Asset Delivery's own three-term vocabulary, reused rather than reinvented: bundled with the initial install; downloaded automatically right after install completes; fetched only when the app actually requests it.

group.description: Build-tool-owned pack/tag identifier (an actual Play asset pack name, an ODR tag, a Background Assets download identifier) — lives in that platform's own build config; this is just the label the staging step threads through, not a spec-level name for either store's tooling.

component.description: Optional (ADR-013). A cartridge-author-defined label for the internal stage/subnet this artifact belongs to, for cartridges that are internally a composed, multi-network pipeline (e.g. a streaming ASR cartridge's separate frontend/encoder/adapter/prefill/step models) rather than one monolithic model. Purely a grouping/selection label for tooling — it does not change how `kind=weights-update` applies: the update's `artifacts` array still explicitly lists every changed file by path+digest, exactly as today; `component` just lets that list, and a `delivery` grouping, be described and filtered by named stage instead of by filename convention alone. No enum: valid values are entirely cartridge-specific, the same way `role: other` and `derived_from.source` are open-ended today.
